articles.title: Starlink Mobile: All the news on SpaceX’s major mobile carrier ambitions
articles.description: SpaceX has declared that it’s going to make Starlink Mobile a “major” mobile carrier. The Elon Musk-owned company has already deployed thousands of direct-to-cell satellites, but its next big challenge is building out its 5G network here on Earth. As part of its plans to rival AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile, SpaceX has inked a deal with Qualcomm, which will deploy its cellular technology across tens of thousands of 5G cell sites starting in 2027. SpaceX is also reportedly in talks to buy Boost Mobile, potentially allowing it to launch Starlink Mobile through the service. Another report suggests SpaceX may tap into 80,000 cell sites across the US to build out its network. SpaceX’s big plans have garnered some reactions in the telecom industry. Tim Höttges, the CEO of T-Mobile’s parent company Deutsche Telekom, said he takes SpaceX’s plans “super serious” but that it could cost Musk more than $200 billion to pull off. Follow along for the latest updates on Starlink’s major mobile carrier ambitions. What will it take for SpaceX to launch its “major” mobile network? articles.title: What Does QUALCOMM (QCOM) Winning A Nationwide 5G Buildout Mean For Investors?
articles.description: QUALCOMM (NasdaqGS:QCOM) and SpaceX have agreed a multiyear partnership to power the new Starlink Mobile nationwide 5G network. The project uses Qualcomm 5G infrastructure technology at national scale, taking the chip designer beyond its traditional smartphone-focused business. Starlink Mobile aims to offer a satellite-backed 5G service across the U.S., creating a new competitor to existing wireless carriers. This Starlink Mobile 5G infrastructure deal with SpaceX is a big swing for Qualcomm...
